title: Redwood + Constellation: Marketplace listing & Reference Architecture sync
summary: Partner technical sync to align on marketplace listing requirements, reference architecture for private deployments, and a joint solution brief. Key concerns: VPC/VPN network connectivity, KMS integration, listing metadata, and joint benchmark plan. Action items and next steps agreed for pricing doc, security pack, and a benchmark run on Constellation testbed.
next_steps: Alex to send draft marketplace listing metadata and screenshots by 2026-07-20
Priya to share reference architecture diagram (v1) and deployment notes by 2026-07-22
Constellation to provide testbed access & sample dataset by 2026-07-24
SE to run initial benchmark and share perf numbers by 2026-07-30
Schedule follow-up on 2026-08-03 to review benchmark and finalize listing
action_items: Alex - Draft marketplace listing metadata + screenshots - due 2026-07-20
Priya - Share reference architecture diagram v1 + notes - due 2026-07-22
Raj - Provide VPC peering details and testbed credentials - due 2026-07-24
Marta - Share SOC2/ISO artifacts and encryption/KMS contacts - due 2026-07-23
Marco - Run model inference benchmark on Constellation testbed and send results - due 2026-07-30
transcript:
[00:00] Alex Tran: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. we got 60 minutes, happy to run through the marketplace listing and the reference arch. um, can I get quick intros?
[00:12] Dana Liu: Sure, Dana from Constellation, partner PM, I'll be owning the marketplace onboarding.
[00:18] Raj Patel: Raj, cloud eng, I'll handle the networking and testbed side.
[00:24] Marta Gomez: Marta, security, hi.
[00:27] Alex Tran: Great, Priya and Marco here on the Redwood side, Priya will cover the reference arch, Marco will help with benchmarks.
[00:34] Priya Desai: hi all. quick agenda: listing metadata, reference arch for private and VPC deploys, joint solution brief, bench plan, and open Q&A.
[00:45] Alex Tran: Kickoff — marketplace listing: Constellation wants Redwood to appear as a managed inference option in your marketplace correct? and include a one-click deploy for dedicated and private?
[00:58] Dana Liu: yes that's right. two listing types: hosted api integration (we call it marketplace-managed) and a reference architecture for our "Bring Your Own infra" reference. we need screenshots, short description, pricing tiers, and an architecture diagram.
[01:12] Alex Tran: Got it. For pricing we'll give tiered pricing guidance and also note reserved capacity commit options — we'll provide a short pricing sheet.
[01:22] Dana Liu: Cool, on the snippet text we need an 80-120 word blurb and a couple of icons.
[01:28] Priya Desai: On the reference arch, here's what we propose: private control plane in your VPC, optional on-prem package for air-gapped, and connectors for KMS/HSM. single-tenant Dedicated clusters for high-throughput workloads, with autoscale.
[01:45] Raj Patel: pause — when you say private control plane in our VPC, do you mean Redwood runs a customer-managed control plane in Constellation's account or you run it in Redwood but with network peering?
[01:56] Priya Desai: good q. we support both. for the marketplace reference arch we recommend the customer-managed control plane pattern: Redwood ships a small control-plane image that lives in your account, all inference traffic can remain on private network. we also support a managed control plane with VPC peering for teams who prefer it.
[02:18] Raj Patel: ok and what about KMS keys? we need to ensure keys never leave our environment.
[02:24] Marco Ruiz: we integrate with AWS KMS and external HSMs, and we support customer-supplied keys via our KMS provider plugin. keys are never exported. there's an audit log per-token for encryption ops.
[02:36] Marta Gomez: Are audit logs SOC2-ready? we need retention settings and tamper-proofing.
[02:42] Priya Desai: we produce structured audit logs and can ship them to your S3 or to your SIEM via secure syslog. retention is configurable; for the reference arch we'll show how to wire up with your log retention policy.
[02:55] Alex Tran: quick note — sometimes our transcripts say KV cach instead of KV cache, ha.
[03:00] Dana Liu: (laughs) noted.
[03:05] Raj Patel: on network egress, we need predictable latency. can Redwood's dedicated pools be pinned to AZs in Constellation?
[03:13] Priya Desai: yes, we can pin Dedicated pools to specific AZs and also do placement constraints. that'll help latency and reduce cross-AZ egress.
[03:24] Raj Patel: good. any guidance on batch sizing and throughput for 2k qps?
[03:30] Marco Ruiz: for 2k qps depends on model size; our recommendation is a mix of batching and KV cache for prefix reuse. we'll provide a workload profile template and batching config. expect to trade some tail-latency for throughput but we'll show configuration to keep p99 under your SLO.
[03:48] Dana Liu: we have a latency SLO of 200ms p95 for short prompts, and support for longer conversations for customers. will that be realistic?
[03:57] Priya Desai: depends on model, instance type, sequence lengths. for smaller models and quantized runtimes we can hit that with dedicated pools. for larger LLMs likely higher. we should run a benchmark on your testbed.
[04:12] Alex Tran: Ok, benchmark plan: Constellation to provide testbed creds and a representative dataset. Marco will run inference with our quantized profile and share perf numbers.
[04:21] Dana Liu: we'll provision testbed by next week.
[04:25] Raj Patel: Regarding marketplace listing — do you have any restrictions for listing artifacts (licenses, logos)?
[04:30] Alex Tran: we need the Constellation logo in SVG and a short trademark blurb. we'll also include a link to the joint solution brief.
[04:40] Marta Gomez: security review — can you summarize your compliance posture? SOC2, ISO, penetration test cadence?
[04:47] Priya Desai: Redwood is SOC2 certified, we have ISO 27001 in progress, annual pentests, and we can share the SOC2 report under NDA. We also have RBAC, SSO (SAML/OIDC), and perimeter hardening guidance for the private control plane.
[05:05] Marta Gomez: Great. for keys, will you use envelope encryption?
[05:09] Marco Ruiz: yes, envelope encryption patterns, customer-managed keys, and we can optionally integrate with your HSM.
[05:16] Dana Liu: Great. other technical notes: we want a one-click deploy for a reference arch template in our marketplace that will spin up the control plane and a sample dedicated cluster. how opinionated is your terraform?
[05:27] Priya Desai: we provide a terraform module and CloudFormation templates for the reference arch; both are parameterized. we'll provide a marketplace-friendly template with sensible defaults.
[05:37] Raj Patel: Any extra operational costs? e.g., metrics retention, logging egress, monitoring agents?
[05:42] Alex Tran: we'll call those out in the listing as optional add-ons — extended observability retention, premium SLA, and support tiers.
[05:50] Dana Liu: ROI story — partners want unit-cost numbers. can you provide per-token cost estimates for the dedicated profile?
[05:57] Marco Ruiz: yes we'll share a cost model spreadsheet; expect quantization, batching, and caching to drive down unit cost. we'll attach sample numbers for a 13B model quantized to int8.
[06:10] Priya Desai: quick interjection — for the reference arch doc we'll include a decision matrix: managed control plane vs customer-managed control plane, with tradeoffs for latency, security, and operational overhead.
[06:24] Raj Patel: that'd be helpful.
[06:28] Alex Tran: Ok, moving to integration checklist: marketplace metadata, screenshots, reference arch diagrams, security pack, pricing & SLAs, and benchmark results.
[06:38] Dana Liu: wanted to flag legal: we have a standard marketplace listing agreement — legal will want to review your terms.
[06:44] Alex Tran: we'll coordinate legal — I'll put my legal contact on the thread.
[06:48] Marta Gomez: on data residency — some customers require data not leave EU. can you pin regions for hosted inference?
[06:55] Priya Desai: yes we support region pinning and can route requests to EU-only clusters for customers in scope.
[07:05] Raj Patel: any limitations on model versions in the marketplace? how do rollouts work?
[07:11] Marco Ruiz: models can be versioned in the catalog. we support canary rollouts, A/B, and automatic fallback policies to compatible model variants if capacity constrained.
[07:22] Dana Liu: for the listing, we want a short "how it works" animated gif. are you able to provide that?
[07:27] Alex Tran: yes we can supply a 20-30s gif showing deploy flow and example API call; we'll add it to the assets pack.
[07:34] Raj Patel: What about support SLAs for marketplace customers? if a customer hits an outage, how does on-call work?
[07:42] Priya Desai: for marketplace-managed listings we can offer standard support; for Dedicated or Private customers we have premium SLA options with 24/7 oncall depending on the tier.
[07:51] Marta Gomez: One security nit: when using customer-managed control plane, we need clear instructions to rotate keys and revoke access quickly.
[07:58] Marco Ruiz: we'll include key rotation scripts and automation in the repo.
[08:03] Dana Liu: Are there any known gotchas with Constellation's marketplace pattern?
[08:08] Raj Patel: our marketplace does not allow background agents that create outbound connections without user approval. need to ensure the control plane behaves accordingly.
[08:16] Priya Desai: we can make the control plane start in a passive mode and only enable outbound connections after admin consent; we'll document that.
[08:25] Alex Tran: Good. time check — about 50 minutes left, but maybe we don't need it all.
[08:31] Dana Liu: can we talk about joint solution brief? we want a short whitepaper describing typical workloads and cost comparisons against CloudMart and NovaEdge.
[08:41] Alex Tran: yes we'll draft a 2-page joint brief and include a competitive matrix.
[08:47] Raj Patel: For benchmark, what telemetry do you need?
[08:51] Marco Ruiz: request and response times, token counts, GPU utilization, tail latency (p90/p95/p99), and memory/KV cache hit rates. also we'd like to capture model artifacts and quantization profile used.
[09:05] Dana Liu: Ok we'll expose a small collector or give read-only access to the metrics for the test run.
[09:11] Priya Desai: we'll need a sample workload — please include conversational and single-turn prompts.
[09:16] Dana Liu: noted.
[09:20] Alex Tran: any regulatory concerns? Marta?
[09:24] Marta Gomez: we need Data Processing Agreement language and clarity on data retention for logs. Also we need ptr to your incident response plan.
[09:33] Priya Desai: we'll share the DPA template and IR runbook excerpt under NDA.
[09:37] Alex Tran: Ok we're nearing the top of the hour — let's recap and call out owners.
[09:41] Dana Liu: recap sounds good.
[09:44] Alex Tran: Recap: Alex sends marketplace metadata and asset pack; Priya shares reference arch diagrams and decision matrix; Marco runs benchmark and cost model; Constellation provides testbed and security artifacts. Follow-up meeting 2026-08-03 to review.
[09:58] Raj Patel: Sounds good.
[10:02] Marta Gomez: thanks everyone.
[10:05] Alex Tran: Thanks all — we'll share notes and action items. Bye.

Note: transcript occasionally has minor transcription errors (e.g., KV cach), filler words and overlap.

End of transcript.
